rootResolution.authority: none. The pane's machine and cwd are a navigation hint. The authority is an ahub project registration read on the same machine.
steps: No focused context, or no space for it: no candidate.
The space's machine layout is not ready: machine_unavailable. Nothing runs and nothing is guessed.
No cwd (a mod pane): no candidate, explicit selection from that machine's registered projects.
Read `ahub projects --json` on that machine through exec(on: machine). A remote cwd is never resolved or tested on the Mac.
Candidates are registered roots that equal the cwd or contain it at a path-segment boundary. A prefix that is not a segment boundary never matches.
Exactly one candidate: shown as the default, still confirmed by the person. Several: ambiguous, the person picks. None: the person picks from the list or sees the setup instruction.
Two registrations with the same root are duplicate: refused until the person resolves it with ahub.

ambiguities.worktree: A git worktree is its own project root (ahub stops at the nearest git working-tree boundary), so a pane in a worktree resolves to the worktree, which may have no hub even if the main checkout has one. The message is the existing `no hub running for <root>`; the companion does not start one.
ambiguities.nestedRegistrations: A cwd under two registered roots (for example a parent folder and a project inside it) is ambiguous; the deepest is highlighted, never chosen.
ambiguities.symlinkedCwd: A pane cwd through a symlink (/tmp versus /private/tmp) may not match a canonical registered root. The unmatched cwd is not canonicalized on the Mac; the person picks.
ambiguities.unregistered: A cwd inside no registration has no candidate. ahub's own rule would use the git root or the folder, but the companion does not register or initialize anything.
ambiguities.staleCwd: The pane may have changed directory since the list was read. Re-read focused() immediately before every effect and compare machine and root; a change refuses with a refresh instruction.
ambiguities.machineRename: A machine name is the host's own label. A name not in machines() is refused; the companion never maps it to this Mac.

rootResolution.referenceImplementation: test/helpers/herdr-root-candidates.ts, a specification by example for H1, not shipped code

installOwnership.mechanism: A mod is a folder `mods/<name>/` with main.js and mod.json under the app home (~/.config/herdr-app, or $HERDR_APP_HOME). The app reads it live. No install, disable or uninstall command exists in `herdr-app --help`, `herdr-app commands` or AGENTS.md.
shippedFiles: optionally keys.json entries the person merges
installOwnership.additiveRule: AGENTS.md: copy the mod folder, never overwrite a name that is taken, merge keys instead of replacing them, run `herdr-app check` on the folder, tell the person before adding a mod that runs programs.
installOwnership.firstSeen: The first time Herdr sees a folder it docks one copy per mod.json into the shown layout; `"place": "none"` docks nothing. H1 uses none so the person's layout is not changed by the copy.
installOwnership.bookkeeping: installed.json, seen.json and shared.json are written by Herdr, not by the companion.
installOwnership.disable: Removing the folder (or changing place) is the only mechanism and is the person's action. Its effect on a copy already shown, and on layout files that named the mod, was not observed. H1's native receipt must record it.
neverTouched: keys.json beyond an additive merge the person approves
installOwnership.check: `herdr-app check <mod folder>` before any claim that a mod works
installOwnership.isolation: Native tests use a scratch HERDR_APP_HOME. This task wrote nothing into the person's profile.
